title: SYSK's Guatemalan Adventure, Part Two
summary: Part two of the Guatemalan adventure episode, in which Josh and Chuck recount their week visiting Cooperative for Education (CO-ED) schools in Guatemala. They describe the computer center model (funded by donor seed money, Microsoft licenses, and student contributions for self-sustainability), the simulated internet and software the kids learn, student success stories (a T-shirt business and a broccoli vs. snow peas profitability study), and Howard Lobb, who moved from the US to Guatemala. Other segments cover a Mayan ceremonial chicken dance, the Neverland-like hotel compound, Gabby the psychologist and facilitator, an orphanage school where a 14-year-old girl runs her household and wants to be a bilingual doctor, Jerry's speech at the Santiago Cooperative School, a principal who fought for girls' education during the civil war, Antigua sightseeing, Ron Zacapa rum, a birthday celebration for Jerry, donor interviews with Michelle McMaster, and calls to text-donate $5 to CO-ED and visit its website.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Howard Lobb
segments.summary: Josh introduces the final part of the Guatemala trip and the second school visit, describing Howard Lobb as a memorable, quirky person the team came to like.

segments.title: How the computer center program works
segments.summary: Howard explains that computer centers target schools with about 200 or more kids, rely on seed donations and partners such as Rotary clubs and Microsoft, and become self-sustaining through student monthly contributions.

segments.title: Computer lessons and simulated internet
segments.summary: The hosts describe the computer labs, which have no real internet but a simulated one, and the Microsoft Office, Carter-style typing, and Movie Maker lessons the children learn.

segments.title: Student success stories: T-shirt business and snow peas study
segments.summary: Howard describes a girls' project that started a real T-shirt business, and students who analyzed broccoli versus snow pea profitability and changed local farmers' minds.

segments.title: Howard Lobb's move to Guatemala and his reflections
segments.summary: The hosts explain that most CO-ED staff are based in Cincinnati and travel to Guatemala, while a few, including Howard, live in-country. Howard talks about the gratitude of communities and the importance of sustainable help over one-time donations.

segments.title: Mayan ceremony and chicken dance at the school
segments.summary: At the computer center inauguration, the team watches traditional dancing with children and a live chicken that is ultimately spared in a symbolic Mayan ritual. Kids then show the team their computer work.

segments.title: Hotel compound and meeting Gabby
segments.summary: The hosts describe their odd hotel compound with statues and a Neverland-like feel, and introduce Gabby, a Guatemalan psychologist who works as a facilitator for CO-ED. Josh's emotional interview with her is previewed.

segments.title: Orphanage school and the textbook presentation
segments.summary: The team visits an orphanage-style school where many children have parents who cannot provide for them. A girl who recites textbook care rules impresses them, and they learn her story: a 14-year-old running her household who wants to become a bilingual doctor.

segments.title: Santiago Cooperative School and Jerry's speech
segments.summary: At the final school, producer Jerry gives a speech to students, her first time on air. The principal of the school is described as having kept the school quietly running during the civil war and advocating for girls' education.

segments.title: Antigua sightseeing and Ron Zacapa rum
segments.summary: The hosts describe Antigua, the former capital until 1776, its earthquake-damaged churches and the arch built for nuns, and their hotel. They also discuss Ron Zacapa rum and a ritual of burning the devil out of the bottle.

segments.title: Donor perspective, walking tour, and final-night celebrations
segments.summary: Donor Michelle McMaster explains why she gives, and the hosts describe the walking tour, shopping with student guides who got gifts for their families, the farewell slideshow, and Jerry's birthday cake.

segments.title: Final thoughts, donation appeal, and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts share final impressions, promote the CO-ED website and Guatemala photo gallery, and ask listeners to text STUFF to 20222 for a five-dollar donation before the campaign ends. They close with the show's sign-off.
